Title: Mom's estate, two siblings, one disagreement. Help?

Hi everyone, long-time lurker, first-time poster. Please be gentle, it's been a rough stretch.

My mother passed away this spring. She left a modest account that my brother and I split equally, and the attorney handling things has now come back with two ways for us to receive it. My brother and I have been talking past each other for a couple of weeks, so I thought I'd get some outside perspective before we sign anything.

A bit about us. I'm a high school librarian, my husband works in facilities for the county, and we have two teenagers. We aren't struggling, but we also aren't flush. My brother lives a few states away, runs a small landscaping company, and has had a bumpy time with cash flow since his main client pulled out. We love each other, but we handle money very differently. He tends to want everything now. I tend to want to wait and see what's offered.

What we both agree on is the following. Whichever payout we choose, the cash is only useful to the household if it lands within {horizon}; after that the reason we need it will have passed. I'm not going to get into the details of what it's for, partly because it's personal and partly because it isn't what I'm asking about. Just take it as given.

The attorney was very clear that both options are legitimate and that there are no hidden fees. She also mentioned that the choice has to be made jointly, which is why we're stuck. I've been reading the posts here for a while and I know there are folks who like to relitigate the whole situation, so I'll pre-empt that: we are not contesting the will, we're not hiring a second lawyer, and we are not going to sell the house. We just need to pick.

Thank you in advance, and thank you to everyone who has helped others here. Some of those threads got me through a hard few weeks.

The two options from the attorney:

{options}

Which of these two should we choose?

Our biggest regular customer, the dental group, has been paying promptly, which helps. Two of our people asked about raises and I told them we would talk once this was settled. I don't want to make promises I can't keep, so I want to know what we can count on before I say anything.

The city's finance office told me, and I wrote this down, that there is no difference in taxes or paperwork between the two arrangements, and that neither one affects my right to appeal anything else. I checked with the lawyer and she said the same.
